andy-hightower-rome-1895-08-03.A1:
FLED UNDER FIRE.
A Negro Shot in Trying to Escape From an Officer of the Law.
Rome, Ga., Aug. 3.—Andy Hightower, a negro wanted in Cedartown and other places, was hot this afternoon by Deputy Sheriff J. K. Williamson and Raymond McConnell. He resisted arrest and tried to escape. Both fired, but the negro kept running, and got into a swamp. He found that he had been struck by a bullet, and thinking he was going to die, returned and gave himself up. Physicians found that the wound was not necessarily fatal and the negro is expected to recover.
andy-hightower-rome-1895-08-03.A2:
HIGHTOWER GONE HIGHER.
Death of the Man Shot by Officers. His Bad Name.
Rome, Ga., Aug. 4—Andy Hightower, the negro shot by officers yesterday afternoon, died this morning at 10 o'clock. A coroners jury was organized, but adjourned till to-morrow to hear more witnesses. Thirty minutes before he died, it is said, one of the physicians in attendance left him and said said he would be able to resume work at the furnace in a few days. Besides being wanted at Cedartown on several warrants, it is said, he was wanted for killing a man at Talladega, Ala. He bore a bad character.

berry-s-brother-unnamed-tippecanoe-1895-.A1:
Killed by a Town Marshal.
CADIZ, O., Aug. 16.—The marshal of New Philadelphia attempted to arrest a colored man named Berry at Tippecanoe to take him to Tuscarrwas county to stand trial for an assault. The colored man and his brother, who had a revolver, resisted arrest, and shooting commenced. The marshal was shot through the wrist, but he succeeded in planting three bullets in the brother's breast, killing him instantly, and the prisoner escaped with a shotgun, and would have killed the marshal, in all probability, but his gun missed fire.
